retries.before:
Fencing in Romsey starts with the ground as much as the timber. On the lower streets towards the River Test, water sits high after prolonged rain, so each post position is checked before a hole is dug. Out at Crampmoor and Highwood, the larger wooded gardens mean longer boundary runs, so the whole line is marked out first and the length is known before anything is ordered. We're a family run, independent team of [CV: team_size].

The work follows a set order. We peg out the run and check for anything buried along it, then the old fence comes down if there is one. Holes are dug, posts are stood and lined up, and only then do the rails and boards or panels go on, because everything hangs off those posts. The gate is hung last, and the cut offs and old timber go with us.

Cutting corners on the posts is where fences let people down. Posts that aren't supported properly move, and once one shifts, the panels either side go out of line with it. Left alone, a loose section keeps working looser until it drops. It's a slow failure, which is why the groundwork matters more than the finish.

We do this work in Romsey ourselves, and you can [see our full fencing service](/services/fencing) for the wider picture.

If a boundary needs replacing or putting in, the length and the style you're after are all we need to start.

svc_block4_h2: Signs It's Time for a Fencing Visit

block4.card_title: Growth has got ahead of you
block4.card_body: Long grass and weeds climb against the base of a fence in the growing season and hold water against the timber. The signs are boards gone soft at ground level, posts that lean and sections that move when pushed. Left alone, trapped moisture keeps working at the wood, and loose sections weaken and fall.

block4.card_title: It looks untidy from the house
block4.card_body: From the window or the back door, a fence that's drifted out of line shows first. Boards come away, panels sit at different heights and the run no longer reads as one boundary. The visit puts that right at the posts: they're set and lined up, then the rails and panels or boards are fixed square to them.

A board nailed back or a post propped up only deals with what shows. Fence timber that sits in wet ground without drainage around it tends to rot early, however often it's patched. The cause is usually how the post was supported at ground level, so a lasting fix means resetting that post, not tidying the symptom.

block4.card_title: What the season is about to throw at it
block4.card_body: Spring growth arrives all at once and hides the foot of the fence. Soft timber or a post that has started to lean can go unnoticed until it's covered. Winter leaves timber wetter than it looks, so getting ahead of it means finding weak sections early, while they're still easy to reach.

steps.step_title: Tell Us What Needs Keeping On Top Of
steps.step_body: Message or call with the boundary length, the fence style you have in mind and any photos. Tell us too if an old fence needs to come out.

steps.step_title: We Agree the Visit and the Price
steps.step_body: We go through what the fencing involves, from taking the old fence out to hanging the gate. Then we agree the cost, so you know the job and its price.

steps.step_title: We Start on a Date That Suits You
steps.step_body: Your fencing job goes in the diary for a date that works for you. The first task on the day is marking out the boundary.

svc_block5_h2: How We Price Fencing Visits in Romsey
svc_cost_intro: What a fencing job costs depends on the boundary itself and on what's standing there now. The cards below set out the main things that move the price, so you can see why two gardens can come out differently.

block5.card_title: What a visit has to get through
block5.card_body: Boundary length is the first thing that moves the price, because a longer run means more posts, more timber and more hours on site. A short, straight run with square corners costs less than a long one that bends around the garden.

block5.card_title: How much is in the way
block5.card_body: Difficult ground and limited access both add time. Ground that's hard to dig slows the post holes, and a narrow way in means materials and waste have to be moved further.

What's already there changes the job. Taking out and clearing an old fence adds work, while sound posts or panels that can be reused take work out. Which applies is clear once the boundary has been looked at.

block5.card_title: Extras you add to the visit
block5.card_body: A gate adds to the job because it has to be hung and fitted square. Work alongside the fence, such as hedge trimming or weed control along the boundary, adds further to the visit.

Fencing is carried out across all of that area, from the lower streets by the River Test to the larger gardens further out.

faq_items.faq_question: How often should fencing be done?
faq_items.faq_answer: Fencing isn't done on a set cycle, so the schedule is agreed with you. The weather decides the timing. Groundwork isn't done when the ground is frozen or too wet to hold a stable post hole. How long a job takes varies with the boundary, so there's no standard time.

faq_items.faq_question: How much does a fencing visit cost in Romsey?
faq_items.faq_answer: Fencing prices are agreed with you for each boundary, and the quote is free. Length is one of the main things that moves the price, along with what's standing there now and how easy the ground is to dig. Once the boundary has been looked at, the figure is clear.

Yes, we're insured up to £[CV: insurance_cover]. That cover applies to the fencing work we carry out, from the first post hole to the last panel. It's there for accidents that can happen while the work is under way, such as damage to a neighbouring panel or a nearby window.

faq_items.faq_question: Do I need to be home for a fencing visit?
faq_items.faq_answer: The arrangements for getting in are agreed before the first visit. If access to the boundary is tight, say so when you first message us. Limited access is one of the things that shapes how the job is planned.

faq_items.faq_question: What does a fencing visit include?
faq_items.faq_answer: A fencing visit runs from marking out the boundary to hanging the gate. We mark the line and check the ground for buried services. Any old fence comes down, then the post holes are dug and the posts set in line. Rails and cladding follow, and the gate goes on last. Work on a hedge beside the fence is a separate service, [hedge trimming](/services/hedge-trimming).

faq_items.faq_question: Are there rules or standards for fencing?
faq_items.faq_answer: Usually no planning permission is needed if the fence stays under a set height. In most cases that's up to two metres, or one metre beside a road used by vehicles. Listed buildings and conservation areas can change that, so check first if yours is one. Ordinary fences don't usually need separate building control approval, but they do have to be built soundly.

faq_items.faq_question: When should I book fencing for the season?
faq_items.faq_answer: Book the first fencing visit of the year early. Winter wind and rain work on posts and panels. That first visit is where failing sections are found and dealt with before they spread. Finding a rotted post early often means replacing one post rather than a whole run.
